newsitem.title: UK: Novo spill dampens June Urals talk, W. Africa firm.
newsitem.headline: Novo spill dampens June Urals talk, W. Africa firm.

text.p: Mediterranean sour crude markets were dulled by news of an oil spill at Russia's main export terminal on the Black Sea but West African grades showed signs of firming as June avails thinned, traders said on Wednesday.

The last two remaining May Russian Urals cargoes were placed on Tuesday at steady discounts of around $1.40 below Dated Brent but talk on June cargoes was slow with traders waiting to see whether the Novorossiisk spill would delay loadings.
"There's been little discussion about June this morning because we're all waiting for more details on the situation at Novorossiisk," said a trader.
Nearly 400 tonnes of oil were spilled at the port when a pipeline burst open on Tuesday night. Russian officials said 13 tonnes had spilled into the sea but the port was still operating.
"From 7 a.m. (0300 GMT), loading of tankers at Novorossiisk port's number one quay was resumed," said a spokesman for the Russian Emergencies Ministry in Moscow.

Traders said loading of the 132,962 dwt Arteaga with one million barrels of Urals would be completed but they were waiting for information about how long the clean-up operation and pipeline repairs would take.

Two ha (5 acres) of the surface of the sea around the 650,000 barrels per day (bpd) terminal were polluted. Booms had been deployed to contain the spill and eight vessels were taking part in the operation.
Meanwhile, West African crudes were looking perkier, helped by a narrower Brent-Dubai spread and healthy interest from refiners in the U.S. Gulf, traders said.
A Nigerian Bonny Light cargo fetched Dated Brent +54 cents in a deal between traders on Tuesday, four cents firmer than the last reported sale.
"There's not much left on an fob basis but there is still a fair bit being offered off VLCCs into the U.S. Gulf," said a trader.
Nigerian Forcados was also firmer after a cargo loading in the third decade of June traded at Dated Brent +24 cents, late last week.
